result.message: Reviewed the submitted candidate (subject_sha256 c31ed578…, equal to the round-1 seed snapshot) against the pinned FlagGems evaluation contract and the optimize ledger. The artifact is a genuine Triton implementation: `run(inp, dim, start, length)` matches the declared ABI (definition params inp/dim/start/length, single output `out`), returns a freshly allocated contiguous tensor, never mutates or aliases `inp`, never falls back to torch/torch.ops, adds no environment mutation, and performs no device synchronization (`inp.shape/stride/dim`, `out.numel()`, `inp.dtype/device` are all metadata; no `.item()`/bool cast of device data). I traced all four kernels by hand: flat copy (pre==1), grid-striding persistent copy, run copy (pre>1, row base stepped by dim_size*post) and the rank-generic strided gather; index arithmetic, EVEN/mask handling, `start`/`length` clamping and negative-`dim`/negative-`start` normalization are consistent with `torch.narrow_copy`, and the `canonical` test conservatively routes exotic-size-1 stride layouts to the strided path (which is still correct for them). The dispatch cannot produce a zero-element grid: any zero input dimension makes `n == 0` and returns early. The record shows 33/33 workloads PASSED in round 1, and the ledger's round-2 PARTIAL_PASS (9 correctness `TypeError`s on the runs-kernel path) belongs to a different, non-submitted sha and was correctly reverted, so it is not a defect of this artifact. Remaining items are advisory: the only unvalidated branch (non-row-major strided gather, using 64-bit vector index arithmetic) plus honest reporting that the accepted 'best' is the unmodified seed and scores below 1.0x on the recorded timing set. The persistent-grid constants (`_PERSIST_THRESHOLD=128`, `_PERSIST_ITERS=13`, grid 40..256) are tuned heuristics for Ascend's block/launch tradeoff, not shape- or value-specific shortcuts, so I do not treat them as cheating.
